what: Avnet distributes electronic components. It buys semiconductors, connectors, passive components and embedded boards from manufacturers and sells them to the companies that build electronic products, holding inventory and providing design and supply chain support along the way.
customers: Electronics manufacturers of every size, from large contract manufacturers to small engineering firms, plus the Farnell business which sells small quantities to engineers and makers online.
money: Distribution of semiconductors, interconnect, passive and electromechanical components.
High-service online distribution of small quantities to engineers and prototype builders.
moat: Distribution is a scale business: holding inventory across hundreds of thousands of part numbers and thousands of customers requires working capital and logistics that smaller competitors cannot match. Component manufacturers need distributors to reach customers too small to serve directly, and those franchise agreements are long-standing.
risks: Margins are extremely thin: about $564.8M of net income on $32.5B of revenue, roughly 1.2%. Small changes in gross margin move profit a great deal.
Free cash flow was about negative $1.1B in the trailing period, because inventory absorbs cash when sales grow. Distribution consumes working capital in upturns and releases it in downturns.
Revenue is cyclical with the semiconductor industry: $26.5B in 2023 down to $22.2B in 2025 then $27.6B.
Debt of $3.5B against $155.4M of cash largely finances inventory and receivables.
Only four analysts cover the stock, so the $111.25 average target rests on minimal coverage.
opportunities: The shares trade at about 11.7 times earnings and 0.20 times sales.
Revenue rebounded sharply to about $27.6B, suggesting the component inventory correction has run its course.
Design support services, where Avnet helps a customer choose and engineer in components, earn higher margins than pure fulfilment.
When the cycle turns down, working capital converts back into cash, which is why distributors can return capital even in weak years.
watch: Gross margin percentage. With net margins near one percent, nothing matters more than the spread Avnet earns between buying and selling a component, and it moves with the supply and demand balance in semiconductors.
